docs.title: Floowandereeze & Modding - Duel Links Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation for Floowandereeze & Modding - Duel Links, a tool for modding the desktop version of Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Links. This documentation will guide you through all the features and capabilities of the application.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
To begin using Floowandereeze & Modding:

  1. Download the application from the Releases page and run the .exe.
  2. Download game assets through Duel Links, then close the game before editing.
  3. Open Configuration and use Auto-detect to select a downloaded Steam account, or select the installation, LocalData, or player folder manually.
  4. Click Check to load the asset metadata. Configuration also supports a different metadata repository, branch, or local ETL checkout.
  5. Open an asset tab to start editing. Tabs become available after a valid path is selected and refresh after a successful metadata update; restarting is unnecessary.

Enable Backups in Configuration before replacing textures to save their originals. The Backups tab is available even without a configured game path.

docs.title: Documentation Sections
docs.text:
Explore the documentation to learn how to use all the features of Floowandereeze & Modding:

  • Configuration - Learn how to configure application settings
  • Card Editor - Customize card art
  • Card Sleeve Editor - Design custom card sleeves
  • Playmat Editor - Create unique playmat textures
  • Character Editor - Search characters and edit one or several character textures
  • Backups - Browse originals, export and import ZIP archives, or remove selected backups

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: If you encounter any issues or have questions about using Floowandereeze & Modding, please check the documentation sections for detailed guides on each feature.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome! If you find a bug or have a feature request, please open an issue on the GitHub repository.

docs.title: Automatic GUI screenshots
docs.text: The root-level capture_docs.py follows the screenshot workflow in floo-qt: it opens the real PySide6 window, switches tabs, selects real game assets, prepares image previews, and saves PNGs. It also captures the character asset dialog.

docs.title: Prepare and run
docs.text:
Configure a downloaded Duel Links account in the app and click Check to populate database.db. Close the game. From the project root, install the runtime dependencies and rebuild generated Qt modules before capturing:

.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt
.\build_qt.ps1
python capture_docs.py

The default command replaces config.png, sleeve.png, card.png, field.png, character.png, character_edit.png, and backups.png in docs/assets/ui/. It prints each destination and writes the Qt version, window mode, selected asset names, and image dimensions to build/docs-captures/manifest.json.

The window maximizes by default and switches tabs automatically. Let it finish without interacting with it. Captures include the application contents, without the operating system's title bar or desktop. Qt captures at the screen's pixel density.

docs.title: Choose pages and output
docs.text:
python capture_docs.py --pages character --character-search "Yugi"
python capture_docs.py --pages card sleeve --card-search "Blue-Eyes"
python capture_docs.py --database local/development.db --output build/review-captures
python capture_docs.py --windowed --width 1600 --height 1000
python capture_docs.py --offscreen --output build/headless-captures

--pages accepts config, sleeve, card, field, character, and backups. The character option saves both the page and its asset dialog. Card search defaults to Blue-Eyes and requires at least three characters. Characters use the first result, optionally narrowed by --character-search; other editors select the first metadata result. The character dialog selects the first asset with a readable texture. Missing metadata or installed textures fail the run instead of creating placeholder previews. Earlier captures can remain after a failure.

--windowed uses the requested logical dimensions (minimum 1280 × 900). --offscreen also uses fixed dimensions and renders without displaying a window; platform fonts and styles can differ from normal Windows captures. Configuration and Backups can be captured without a game path:

python capture_docs.py --pages config backups --offscreen

docs.title: Isolation and review
docs.text:
The helper opens the source SQLite database read-only and uses SQLite's backup API to make a consistent temporary copy under build/. Application migrations and configuration callbacks affect only that copy. Qt settings and temporary images are isolated in the same disposable directory. It reads the project's real backup inventory for display. It never invokes Replace, Restore, Check, Import, or Remove.

Configuration displays generic account and local metadata paths and clears the custom background; the actual game path remains available internally for reading textures. Review screenshots before publishing: metadata source settings, backup filenames, and asset names reflect your local data. Installed mods and missing game downloads also affect the pictures.

The editor source previews reuse their selected installed artwork through the normal image-loading handler. Current and replacement previews intentionally show the same artwork; no mod is applied. Example images are removed with the temporary copy.

To review separately before replacing documentation pictures:

python capture_docs.py --output build/review-captures
# Inspect the PNGs, then copy the reviewed pictures.
Copy-Item build/review-captures/*.png docs/assets/ui/
python -m mkdocs build --strict --site-dir build/docs-preview

When --output is supplied, its manifest is saved alongside its PNGs.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
Open Backups in the navigation toolbar to manage the saved originals in the app's local backups/ folder. This page works before a game path is configured. Open the page or click Refresh to rescan files after editing assets.

The table shows each file's category, relative path, and size. Known categories are Cards, Sleeves, Fields, and Characters; other folders are listed by their folder names.

docs.title: Choose backups
docs.text:
Use Category to filter the table, then choose an Action scope:

  • Everything includes all files, including categories hidden by the filter.
  • Current category includes every file in the chosen category. Choose a specific category first.
  • Selected backups includes highlighted rows. Use Ctrl-click or Shift-click to select multiple files.

docs.title: Export and import
docs.text:
Click Export ZIP… to save the chosen scope to an archive. Export preserves paths relative to backups/ and leaves local files in place.

Click Import ZIP…, choose an archive, then choose everything, a category, or individual files in the preview. Click Import. For existing files, choose Yes to replace them, No to keep them and import only new files, or Cancel to stop.

Archives should contain category folders directly, such as cards/12345678.png, without an extra backups/ folder. Use backups created for Duel Links; archives from other games may contain unrelated files. Importing stores backups locally. Apply an original through the relevant editor's restore control or Restore All in Configuration.

Unsafe paths, duplicate paths, symbolic links, and archives larger than 4 GiB or 100,000 files are rejected. Selected files are checked before local files change. A disk or write failure can still leave a partial import; resolve the failure, refresh, and retry.

docs.title: Remove backups
docs.text:
Choose a scope, click Remove backups…, and confirm the file count. Removal is permanent, so export files you may need first. Importing and removing backups updates backup indicators in loaded asset lists. Neither action changes game files.

Archives contain saved originals only, without settings, metadata, or game installations. Enable automatic backup creation in Configuration before editing assets; it does not create originals retroactively.

docs.title: Card Editor
docs.text: The Card Editor page allows you to modify card art in Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Links. This page provides functionality to view, replace, and manage card textures.

docs.title: Resizing and image fitting
docs.text:
Resize the window to scale the Current and Preview images. Drag the dotted divider between the editor and results to change their relative heights; the app remembers this position and the window size. Results wrap into columns as space becomes available. On smaller windows, scroll the editor to reach its controls.

Select or drop an image, then choose Stretch or Crop. In Crop mode, drag the crop rectangle or its corner handles. Your crop stays in place when the window resizes.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Card list with search functionality
  • Card preview and editing
  • Card art replacement
  • Card texture extraction
  • Backup and restore functionality
  • Auto-complete search suggestions

docs.title: Card List
docs.text:
• Displays all available cards in a thumbnail view
  • Click on a card to select it for editing
  • Shows card names below thumbnails

docs.title: Preview Section
docs.text:
• Shows the currently selected card's art
  • Displays the card's bundle information
  • Updates in real-time when changes are made

docs.title: Action Buttons
docs.text:
• Select Image: Choose a new card art image
  • Replace: Apply the selected image to the card
  • Copy: Copy the card bundle to the cards folder
  • Extract: Extract the card's texture
  • Restore: Restore the card from backup
  • Favorite: Mark/unmark the selected card as favorite

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
• Search box with auto-complete suggestions
  • Minimum 3 characters required for search
  • Case-insensitive search
  • Favorites: Filter to show only favorited cards
  • Matches partial text within card names

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Searching Cards

    • Type at least 3 characters in the search box
    • Use auto-complete suggestions for quick selection
    • Check "Favorites" to filter only favorited cards
    • The list will filter to show matching cards after clicking the search button or pressing ENTER

  2. Selecting a Card

    • Click on a card in the list to select it
    • The preview will update to show the selected card
    • Action buttons will become enabled

  3. Replacing Card Art

    • Click "Select Image" to choose a new card art, or drag and drop an image
    • Preview the selected image
    • Click "Replace" to apply the changes
    • A backup will be created if enabled in settings

  4. Managing Backups

    • Select a modified card
    • Click "Restore" to revert to the original version
    • A notification will indicate if backup exists

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The application creates backups automatically if enabled in settings
  • Unity3D cards cannot be copied but can be extracted
  • The search feature requires at least 3 characters to prevent performance issues
  • Pendulum cards are currently not supported due to the complexity of their art
  • Rush Duel cards are currently not supported due to the complexity of their art

docs.title: Character Editor
docs.text: Open Characters to browse the character metadata downloaded through Configuration. Select a character to enable its Favorite control, or double-click to open its assets.

docs.title: Find a character
docs.text: Type a name in Search characters. Results update after a short pause; Enter searches immediately. Search works together with the series selector and Favorites filter. The Clear button beside the series filter resets all three. Characters are ordered by series and name; missing names appear as Character <ID>. Hover over a thumbnail for its full name.

docs.title: Edit character assets
docs.text:
1. Double-click a character, then choose All Assets, Duel Assets, Dialog Assets, or Miscellaneous in Filter by type.
  2. Select an asset to view its installed texture. Use Ctrl-click or Shift-click for multiple selections, Select All for the current list, or Clear to deselect.
  3. Choose Select Image or drop an image into the dialog. The source preview shows the replacement before you apply it.
  4. Choose Stretch to resize the image to the target texture, or Crop to select the source area. Drag the crop rectangle or its handles to adjust it.
  5. Click Replace Asset, or Replace N Assets for a selection of several assets.

For one asset, Crop uses its visible content proportions when those can be read. For multiple assets, the crop is freeform and shared by the selection. Each target fits the selected area into its original content bounds, preserving transparent margins and texture dimensions. Stretch resizes to the whole texture.

docs.title: Extract, restore, and back up
docs.text:
Extract Asset saves the selected textures under images/characters/. Restore Asset restores selected textures with saved originals. Both actions also work on multiple selections; their button labels show the selection count. An action reports any assets that failed, so check the result before continuing.

With automatic backups enabled, replacement saves each bundle's original texture under backups/characters/. Editing the same bundle again keeps the existing original. Use Backups to export or import these files, and Configuration for Restore All.

Only assets listed in the metadata and downloaded in the selected game account can be previewed or edited. If a preview is unavailable, check the account path, download the assets in Duel Links, and refresh metadata with Check.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The Configuration page allows you to manage application settings and perform maintenance tasks in Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Links. This page provides functionality to configure game paths, update data, manage backups, and customize the application appearance.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Steam game discovery and manual game path configuration
  • Data update management
  • Backup system configuration
  • Application appearance customization
  • Asset compression settings
  • Mipmap count configuration
  • Bulk backup management

docs.title: Game Path Settings
docs.text:
• Auto-detect: Find Duel Links accounts across your Steam libraries and select the account to use
  • Game Path: Select a Duel Links installation, its LocalData folder, or a player ID folder
  • Check Button: Check and update app data
  • Version Display: Show current data version

docs.title: Metadata Source
docs.text:
• Metadata source: GitHub repository in owner/repository format, or a local repository folder. The default is Nauder/floowandereeze-and-modding-etl-dl.
  • Browse local…: Select the root of a local ETL checkout containing data/version.txt and the four asset Parquet files.
  • Metadata branch: GitHub branch or ref to download. Leave blank to use the repository's default branch. Disabled for local sources.
  • Save source: Save these settings for future checks.
  • Use defaults: Restore the default repository and clear the branch override.

To test the asset-name branch, enter feat/local-game-asset-names in Metadata branch, then click Check. Check saves the source fields and downloads all asset datasets from that source. Switching sources refreshes the data even when the version dates match. The previous successful source and version are kept if a download fails. To return to the default data, click Use defaults, then Check.

For local testing, click Browse local…, select your ETL repository, then click Check. The app reads files from the current working tree, including uncommitted changes, without contacting GitHub. Each local check reloads all four datasets even when version.txt has not changed. Rerun the ETL export and click Check to test new data; committing or publishing it is unnecessary. Missing files are reported before the source is saved.

docs.title: Backup Management
docs.text:
• Enable Backups: Toggle automatic backup creation
  • Restore All: Restore all modified assets with backups to their original state
  • Clear Backups: Delete all backup files

Use the Backups tab to browse saved originals, export or import ZIP archives, or remove selected backups.

docs.title: Appearance Settings
docs.text:
• Background Image: Set custom application background
  • Reset Background: Remove custom background

docs.title: Asset Settings
docs.text:
• Mipmap Count: Configure texture mipmap levels (Default 10)
  • Compression Options:
  • None
  • LZMA
  • LZ4
  • LZ4HC
  • LZHAM

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Setting Game Path

    • Click "Auto-detect" beside the game path and select a downloaded account
    • You can also select the installation, LocalData folder, or player folder manually
    • When several accounts are available, choose the one to edit
    • Path is validated before being saved; asset tabs become available immediately

  2. Updating Data

    • Set game path first
    • Click "Check" to check for new data
    • Updates are downloaded automatically if available

  3. Managing Backups

    • Toggle "Enable Backups" to control automatic backup creation
    • Use "Restore All" to revert all changes
    • Use "Clear Backups" to remove backup files

  4. Customizing Appearance

    • Click "Select Background" to choose custom background
    • Use "Reset Background" to remove custom background
    • Changes are applied immediately
    • The app has a dark theme, so bright backgrounds are not recommended

  5. Configuring Asset Settings

    • Set desired mipmap count (default: 10)
    • Choose compression method for new assets
    • Settings affect all new asset replacements

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Game path must be set before using most features
  • Data updates require a valid game path first
  • Backup system affects all asset types
  • Asset settings affect all new replacements
  • Asset tabs load when first opened and refresh after successful data updates
  • Backups create local copies of assets, so they take storage space
  • Backgrounds can be stretched to fit or cropped to cover the window while preserving proportions

docs.title: Playmat Editor
docs.text: The Playmat Editor page allows you to modify playmat textures in Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Links. This page provides functionality to view, replace, and manage playmat assets.

docs.title: Resizing and image fitting
docs.text:
Resize the window to scale the Current and Preview images. Drag the dotted divider between the editor and results to change their relative heights; the app remembers this position and the window size. Results wrap into columns as space becomes available. On smaller windows, scroll the editor to reach its controls.

Select or drop an image, then choose Stretch or Crop. In Crop mode, drag the crop rectangle or its corner handles. Your crop stays in place when the window resizes.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Playmat list with preview
  • Playmat texture replacement
  • Automatic backups of both playmat bundles when backups are enabled
  • Texture extraction
  • Bundle copying
  • Real-time preview updates

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Type at least three characters of an asset name or bundle ID, then press Enter or click Search. Suggestions match any part of a name. Clear the search box to show all results again. Asset names appear below the thumbnails; hover for the full name and bundle ID. Unnamed assets display their bundle ID.

Use Check on the Configuration page after upgrading to download the new asset names. Existing favorites and backup flags for sleeves and playmats are kept.

docs.title: Playmat List
docs.text:
• Displays all available playmats
  • Click on a playmat to select it for editing
  • Shows the playmat bundle information

docs.title: Preview Section
docs.text:
• Shows the currently selected playmat
  • Displays the playmat's bundle information
  • Updates in real-time when changes are made

docs.title: Action Buttons
docs.text:
• Select Image: Choose a new playmat texture image
  • Replace: Apply the selected image to the playmat
  • Copy: Copy the playmat bundle to the fields folder
  • Extract: Extract the playmat texture

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Enable backups in Configuration to save the original small and medium playmat textures under backups/fields/ before replacement. Existing backups are kept when replacing the same playmat again. Use Configuration's Restore all action to restore backed-up textures, or the Backups page to export and import them.

  1. Selecting a Playmat

    • Click on a playmat in the list to select it
    • The preview will update to show the selected playmat
    • Action buttons will become enabled

  2. Replacing Playmat Texture

    • Click "Select Image" to choose a new playmat texture
    • Preview the selected image
    • Click "Replace" to apply the changes

  3. Extracting Textures

    • Select a playmat
    • Click "Extract" to save the texture
    • The texture will be saved to the "fields" folder

  4. Copying Playmats

    • Select a playmat
    • Click "Copy" to save the bundle
    • The playmat will be copied to the "fields" folder

docs.title: Card Sleeve Editor
docs.text: The Card Sleeve Editor page allows you to modify card sleeves in Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Links. This page provides functionality to view, replace, and customize card sleeves with optional border effects.

docs.title: Resizing and image fitting
docs.text:
Resize the window to scale the Current and Preview images. Drag the dotted divider between the editor and results to change their relative heights; the app remembers this position and the window size. Results wrap into columns as space becomes available. On smaller windows, scroll the editor to reach its controls.

Select or drop an image, then choose Stretch or Crop. In Crop mode, drag the crop rectangle or its corner handles. Your crop stays in place when the window resizes.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Card sleeve list with preview
  • Sleeve texture replacement
  • Texture extraction
  • Border customization
  • Backup and restore functionality
  • Real-time preview updates

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Type at least three characters of an asset name or bundle ID, then press Enter or click Search. Suggestions match any part of a name. Clear the search box to show all results again. Asset names appear below the thumbnails; hover for the full name and bundle ID. Unnamed assets display their bundle ID.

Use Check on the Configuration page after upgrading to download the new asset names. Existing favorites and backup flags for sleeves and playmats are kept.

docs.title: Card Sleeve List
docs.text:
• Displays all available card sleeves
  • Click on a sleeve to select it for editing

docs.title: Preview Section
docs.text:
• Shows the currently selected card sleeve
  • Displays the selected sleeve's bundle information
  • Updates in real-time when changes are made
  • Supports border preview toggle

docs.title: Action Buttons
docs.text:
• Select Image: Choose a new sleeve texture image
  • Replace: Apply the selected image to the sleeve
  • Copy: Copy the sleeve bundle to the sleeves folder
  • Extract: Extract the sleeve texture
  • Border Color: Choose a color for the sleeve border
  • Restore: Restore the sleeve from backup

docs.title: Border Options
docs.text:
• Checkbox to toggle border
  • Color picker for border customization
  • Border width is set to 15 pixels
  • Fade is available when the border is enabled. It applies the border fade during replacement; the preview shows a simple border rather than the final fade.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Selecting a Card Sleeve

    • Click on a sleeve in the list to select it
    • The preview will update to show the selected sleeve
    • Action buttons will become enabled

  2. Replacing Sleeve Texture

    • Click "Select Image" to choose a new sleeve texture
    • Preview the selected image
    • Click "Replace" to apply the changes
    • A backup will be created if enabled in settings

  3. Customizing Border

    • Click "Border Color" to choose a color
    • Use the checkbox to toggle border preview
    • The border will be applied when replacing the sleeve

  4. Extracting Textures

    • Select a sleeve
    • Click "Extract" to save the texture
    • The texture will be saved to the "sleeves" folder

  5. Managing Backups

    • Select a modified sleeve
    • Click "Restore" to revert to the original version
    • A notification will indicate if backup exists

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The application creates backups automatically if enabled in settings
  • Border customization is optional and can be toggled on/off
